answer: Recursive Terrace Binding. Each agent must place its identity at a unique vertex in a shared, rate-limited naming tree; every new registration re-prices the whole subtree above it and pays that delta to prior occupants. Attackers flooding identities push a rising tide of rent onto their own clusters, since each added node raises the marginal cost of its siblings. Cost scales with cluster width, not single-account price, making mass registration pay continuously.
